title: Adaptive coverage-gating and quarantine orchestrator for hybrid A/B + shadow rollouts
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Goal: Build an adaptive gating layer that combines coverage-weighted eval scorecards with statistical drift detection to protect user traffic during hybrid A/B + shadow rollouts. When a model crosses a configurable risk threshold we should immediately: 1) route affected traffic into quarantine mode (stable model fallback + circuit breaker), 2) create a high-fidelity alert and incident ticket, and 3) start automated remediation actions (automated canary revert or throttled rollback) if configured by the customer.

Background: Current rollback heuristics rely on simple delta thresholds and uniform prompt sets. We frequently see blind spots where regressions happen for low-frequency-but-high-criticality prompts (e.g., legal, payment flows). This ticket implements: (a) coverage-weighted scoring to amplify coverage gaps in scorecards, (b) transient-detection using CUSUM + bootstrap confidence to reduce false positives, and (c) a quarantine orchestration mode that isolates impacted traffic without impacting global SLOs.

Proposal summary:
- Inputs: per-request metadata (route, customer tier, prompt category), eval scorecard results for the prompt families, historical baseline metrics per-model/version, and live sampling from shadowed traffic.
- Scoring: compute per-prompt and per-family weighted deltas where weight = importance*(1 + 1/coverage_fraction). Importance values come from scorecard tags (e.g., "safety", "billing", "fact-check"). Coverage fraction is recent coverage in production for that prompt family.
- Detection: run CUSUM on weighted-delta time series with bootstrap-estimated control limits. Trigger is a sustained exceedance for a configurable window (default 5m contiguous).
- Quarantine mode: automatically route affected user slices to the stable model variant and continue running the candidate model in shadow for data capture. Quarantine includes: prefixed logs, increase in eval sampling rate for impacted prompts, and a temporary rate cap on candidate model.
- Remediation options (configurable per-customer): auto-revert to previous version, throttle candidate to 1% and escalate to manual review, or continue shadowed sampling for 24h with elevated telemetry.

Why this is different: rather than a single global threshold this enforces prompt-family-aware protections so low-volume critical prompts are not drowned by average-case metrics. The quarantine mode provides a fast, low-latency safety valve that is less disruptive than full rollback while giving SRE/ML teams immediate time-series and examples to diagnose.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Reduce time-to-detection for high-severity prompt-family regressions by 50% in internal replay tests.
- False positive rate < 3% on historical backtests (across last 18 months of canaries).
- Automatic quarantine actions can be enacted within 30s of detection in 95% of simulated events.
- Clear telemetry on per-customer gate decisions visible in Console within runtime-1.23 release.
acceptance_criteria: CUSUM + bootstrap detector integrated into rollout orchestrator
Quarantine routing path implemented with fallback to stable model
End-to-end integration tests that simulate prompt-family regressions (small/large), assert auto-quarantine and subsequent actions
Dashboard in Console showing per-prompt-family gate state, recent triggers, and example payloads (sanitized)
Playbook automation: failures create incident, open a rollback PR, and optionally execute configured auto-revert
